audio_caption: The audio begins with a male speaker expressing exhaustion with the length of the show, leading into a discussion about an upcoming match between Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar. He jokes about nearly getting a "are you still there" notification due to the show's length. The speaker continues to describe Paul Heyman introducing Roman Reigns, and indicates "it's every", followed by the audio ending abruptly.

The clip begins with a male speaker expressing enthusiasm for Paul Heyman, followed by a description of Heyman's role in introducing Roman Reigns, specifying him as the "undisputed reigning defending" champion, and mentioning that he gives the microphone back.  Immediately after, the speaker mentions Brock taking the microphone away. The speech is delivered with excitement.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker explaining that "they put Paul Heyman with Brock Lesnar for the first time 20 years ago specifically because Brock wasn't very good at talking, and Paul Heyman was." The speaker continues to describe how Brock learned and improved, noting that "it's a Paul Heyman invitation and it's gold," said with enthusiasm.

The audio begins with two male speakers discussing an event involving Brock, noting its ironic nature and mentioning his prior performance on Raw. They discuss Brock's dissatisfaction with a previous performance. One speaker mimics Brock's statement: "That sucked, I'm never going to do that again." Then, they note that he repeated the performance shortly after. The other male speaker continues, quoting, "Cowboy Country ass-kicker who's gonna kick your ass.  Barrack Lesner." He also references "Roman" and "Hayman", noting Hayman's "butt hurt" reaction to an imitation. The audio ends with the other speaker talking about their past friendship and betrayal.

The clip begins with a male speaker discussing a match, referring to it as the "biggest match in WrestleMania history" and a "heavyweight championship match". The speaker references past matches and mentions specifics like "Suplex City", adopting a conversational tone. The speaker continues by stating an observation about third time ever.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker recounting the origin of the phrase "Suplex City," mentioning it was during a WrestleMania match against Roman Reigns in San Francisco. He states that Brock Lesnar declared "Suplex City, bitch," marking the phrase's birth, and comments that seven years later, they have reached the end of the tale. The speaker's tone is conversational and slightly enthusiastic.

The audio clip features one male speaker describing a wrestling match in an excited, energetic tone. He narrates the sequence of events, including "spears and F-5s and Superman punches and suplexes," along with specific details such as a low blow, a belt shot, and an attempted spear into a kimura. The speaker emphasizes the intense emotions, noting the animosity between the wrestlers and the urgency of the situation. He highlights significant moments, such as one wrestler pleading with his "tribal chief" and another's eyes bulging out of his head. The speaker concludes by describing a final spear, leading to a clean win after years of struggle.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker stating "This was a main event of the biggest show of the year." He is followed by another male speaker who characterizes the event as exactly what he expected, and proceeds to describe the wrestling match emphasizing a sequence of big moves and reversals, contrasting it with another match. He concludes that some may dislike the match, but he considered it a good WrestleMania main event, and feels it delivered as expected.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker expressing his enjoyment of a match, describing it as a "clubbering" between "two big dudes." He suggests that viewers were expecting too much. Another male speaker then asks "What'd you think, Mark?" The second speaker is interrupted by another male speaker who remarks on seeing a character getting punched in the genitals.

The clip opens with a conversation, starting with one speaker who says, "why don't they just wear cups?" and "you'll get punched in the dick and it'll still hurt but not as much." Then, another male speaker responds, saying that if you get punched in the dick with a cup on, it'll "cut your dick off." Someone says, "I just watched Jackass, cups are not foolproof." Another male voice chimes in, stating "Exactly Vinnie, right?", followed by an admission that "I don't think you're gonna get your dick cut off."  A speaker notes that when he was in school, he learned that "the cup goes goes over everything. and so if you kick the cup up, it just the right angle, it's gonna cut your dick off." Another speaker exclaims "bro!" and replies "spoken like a man who never actually played sports." A second voice retorts "spoken like a man who never wore a cup", and admits, "I never wore a cup in my life, I didn't wear a cup wrestling, I didn't wear a cup doing jujitsu, I never wore a cup." One speaker says, "and I never no one ever got me in the balls, cause I avoided it". Another speaker responds in surprise, "Oh, yes," and adds "just stealthy." The other person concurs, "Exactly."

The audio clip features two male speakers discussing a wrestling match. The first man expresses his dissatisfaction, saying the match was "fine" and "the same old match" he's seen before, criticizing its predictability with suplexes, German suplexes, and spears, noting that the wrestler's glove, shoes, and underpants matched. The second speaker acknowledges seeing similar matches at Wrestlemania and in Saudi Arabia, with the first man reiterating, "I've seen that match," in a sarcastic tone.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker inquiring about Roman's next challenger. Another male offers "Austin Theory" as a suggestion, followed by a third male mentioning "Drew McIntyre."  A fourth male sarcastically remarks "Edge".  The first male expresses disbelief, mentioning that the suggested challengers are heels.  The fourth male emphasizes "The Edge Lords" and a conversation starts about the possibility of Edge versus the Bloodline. The first male suggests Theory should be able to work both shows, as he is the dual champion, and should not just be on Smackdown.  A female speaker wonders if he will have both belts until the next Wrestlemania. The clip ends with a male speaker stating that this match has been planned for months.

The audio features a male speaker discussing a wrestling match, questioning the announcer's description of the winner who was already the champion. He references "undisputed WWE Universal champion" and expresses frustration that the wrestlers were referred to by the same title they had going into the match. Towards the beginning of the audio, another male speaker says "they have".

The audio clip begins with one male speaker expressing disappointment, noting the lack of change, "I thought they'd have like a new belt, they'd have a new name," and that they just "stumbled through" calling him the same thing and he now holds both belts. Another male speaker replies, referring to their own Twitter account and says "Through their own Twitter here." The first male speaker acknowledges this and asks, "Oh they got an answer now?" The second male speaker then says "Well, you're not gonna like it."

The audio clip starts with a male speaker announcing that "the tribal chief Roman Reigns has finally defeated Brock Lesnar on the grandest stage of them all to become the undisputed WWE universal champion" with an excited tone. A second male speaker expresses surprise with a simple "Wow." The first speaker then speculates if the victory means Reigns is both WWE and Universal champion. Another male speaker interjects, suggesting "World Champ." The first speaker then asks what's "bigger than a universe," and a third male responds, "nothing, dude." Then the first speaker suggests "a multiverse," and the second speaker follows up with, "Ah, he is the multiverse champion." A fourth male speaker approves. Another speaker jokingly suggests that when he fights someone on Mars, he can be, and then says "this is dumb, just calling the World Champion." Finally, a speaker says that this conversation is "super dumb."

The audio clip begins with an enthusiastic greeting directed to an audience. A male speaker, in an excited tone, urges listeners to visit WWE's Twitter to view a picture depicting Brock holding Roman in a Kimura hold, emphasizing the intensity reflected in Brock's eyes, which he describes as "universal." Following the speaker's message, the sound of retweeting is heard.

The audio begins with a male speaker enthusiastically stating, "It's Brock! Brock's awesome." Another male speaker affirms, "Brock is the best." The first speaker agrees that "this is the best Brock there's ever been" and refers to a "babyface cowboy." He acknowledges Brock's consistent greatness, reiterating that "this is the best Brock." A third male speaker introduces a book about bats, noting that "a bat cannot stand and then take off." Instead, "a bat can only fall from a great height and then fly." He then makes a comparison, stating "Sting is now a bat" and "he just goes up on something really high and he falls." Another male speaker agrees, "He did not jump through these tables. He fell." The conversation transitions into an advertisement spoken by a male, promoting a subscription service offering full-length editions of shows for a monthly fee and including archived shows "all in beautiful HD." The audio concludes with music that sounds electronic and upbeat, seemingly suitable as backing music for a video game or technological presentation.
